questions.question: Which formula defines the Riemann sum?
For $f(x) = 2$ on an interval split into subintervals with total length $5$, what is the Riemann sum?
What does $|J_i|$ represent in a Riemann sum?
options: The value of $f$ at the sample point $x_i^*$
The number of subintervals in the partition
The length of the subinterval $J_i$
The length of the whole interval $I$

questions.question: What does a Riemann sum of $f$ over $[a,b]$ approximate?
options: The definite integral of $f$ over $[a,b]$
The derivative of $f$ at a point of $[a,b]$
The arc length of the graph of $f$
An antiderivative $F$ of $f$ on the interval $[a,b]$

questions.question: Which choices can make two Riemann sums for the same function differ?
options: The choice of partition or of sample points $x_i^*$
The order in which the rectangles are added up
Only the choice between left and right endpoint tags
Only whether the subintervals are open or closed

questions.question: For $f(x)=x$ on $[0,1]$ with one subinterval and sample point $x_1^*=1$, what is $S(f,P_1)$?
For $f(x)=x^2$ on $[0,1]$, use two equal subintervals and right endpoints. What is the Riemann sum?
In a Riemann sum $S(f,P)=\sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*)(x_i-x_{i-1})$, which tags $x_i^*$ are allowed?
options: Any $x_i^*\in[x_{i-1},x_i]$, chosen independently for each $i$
Only the midpoint of each subinterval $[x_{i-1},x_i]$
All left endpoints or all right endpoints, one rule for every $i$
Any point of $[a,b]$, not necessarily in $[x_{i-1},x_i]$

questions.question: When Riemann sums of $f\colon[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ are formed, what does the assumption that $f$ is bounded guarantee?
options: Each piece has a finite supremum and infimum, so $U(f,P)$ and $L(f,P)$ exist.
Each tagged sum $S(f,P)$ is a finite number, which could fail otherwise.
The tags $x_i^*$ can be chosen independently of one another.
The widths $x_i-x_{i-1}$ of the subintervals are finite.

questions.question: Let $f$ be Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$. How do different tagged Riemann sums relate to $\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$?
options: All tagged sums on one partition equal the integral exactly.
Different tag rules tend to different limits, whose average is the integral.
Finite sums may differ, but all tend to the integral as the mesh shrinks.
Only left and right sums tend to the integral; other tags may not.

questions.question: For $f(x)=x$ on $[-1,1]$, take the regular subdivision into $2$ pieces and left endpoints as tags. What is the Riemann sum?
For a regular subdivision of $[0,6]$ into $3$ subintervals, what is the common width?
Let $f$ be Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$, and let $P'$ be obtained from a partition $P$ by adding points. Which statement is always true?
options: $U(f,P')\le U(f,P)$ and $L(f,P')\ge L(f,P)$
$U(f,P')\ge U(f,P)$ and $L(f,P')\le L(f,P)$
Each tagged sum on $P'$ is closer to the integral than each one on $P$.
Each tagged sum on $P'$ is at least as large as each one on $P$.
